key_insight: The ANGLE trial will test whether hyperangulated video laryngoscope blades improve first-attempt intubation success compared with standard-geometry blades.
clinical_relevance: The findings could inform blade selection for emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults.
method: Pragmatic, multicenter, unblinded, parallel-group randomized trial.
Planned enrollment of 2,500 adults across 10 emergency departments and 18 intensive care units in the United States.
Primary outcome: first-attempt intubation success; secondary outcome: hypoxemia during intubation.
evidence_signal: This protocol reports no comparative results; enrollment began December 30, 2025, and is expected to conclude in 2027.
watch_item: The unblinded design may allow operator expectations to influence performance; this is a device-comparison trial, not an AI study.
paper_title: Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for the Hyperangulated versus Standard Geometry Laryngoscope Blade (ANGLE) Trial
